subject: Chemistry
title: Why Onions Make You Cry
description: A quick win: understand Why Onions Make You Cry.

hook.text: When you cut an onion, it releases a gas that turns into sulfuric acid on contact with your eyes.

buildup.text: Cutting breaks onion cells, releasing an enzyme that converts sulfur compounds into a volatile gas.

discovery.text: The gas, syn-propanethial-S-oxide, reacts with water in your tears to form a mild sulfuric acid.

twist.text: Your eyes make more tears to flush the acid. That's why you cry—it's a defensive chemical reaction.

climax.text: Chill the onion before cutting. Cold slows the enzyme and reduces the gas released.

punchline.text: Sulfur gas meets eye water. Acid forms. You cry. Chemistry.

quiz.question: Why do onions make you cry?
options: A sulfur gas reacts with eye moisture to form a mild acid
Onion juice directly irritates the cornea
Onions release pollen that triggers allergies

details.summary: Cutting an onion ruptures cells that release the enzyme alliinase, which converts sulfur compounds into syn-propanethial-S-oxide, a volatile lachrymatory agent..
details.whyItMatters: Onion chemistry is a vivid example of how plants use sulfur-based chemical defense systems. Understanding the mechanism has led to engineered low-tear onion varieties.
takeaways: Cutting onions releases a volatile sulfur compound that irritates eyes
The compound converts to mild sulfuric acid on contact with eye moisture
Chilling onions slows the enzymatic reaction and reduces gas release

faq.question: Why does chilling an onion before cutting reduce tears?
faq.answer: Cold temperatures slow the activity of the alliinase enzyme that produces the tear-causing compound. The reduced enzyme activity means less syn-propanethial-S-oxide is released into the air. Lower temperature also decreases the volatility of the gas, reducing how quickly it reaches your eyes.

faq.question: Have scientists created onions that do not make people cry?
faq.answer: Yes. In 2008, Japanese and New Zealand researchers used gene silencing to create a tearless onion by disabling the lachrymatory factor synthase gene. These onions still contain flavor compounds but redirect the sulfur pathway away from producing the specific tear-causing molecule.
